issue_title: VS Code Not Initializing Angular Language Features in Angular 19
author: aashif-sajah
comment_body:
Hey @atscott ,

Thanks for your time! It turned out to be a permission issue related to the Angular cache. I resolved it by manually deleting the .angular folder and clearing the cache with:

```npx ng cache clean
npm cache clean --force
```

Then, I reinstalled dependencies and restarted the project. Everything is working fine now. 

I appreciate the help, and thanks for your support! 🙌

issue_title: Angular 19: Issue with Style Flickering When Switching Views (ng serve)
author: joewIST
comment_body:
We still get the flickering on Firefox (which occurs while the styles are loaded). The only difference is that on Firefox, once the styles have been loaded, they are not reloaded whenever the component is reused. On Edge/Chrome, they seem to be loaded every time the component is requested, which causes the flicker to occur a lot.

For reference, this is only happening when a) a component is dynamically rendered (e.g. something in a dropdown that gets initialised when the dropdown is opened or b) a component is wrapped in an @if block and is only rendered after a user interaction (e.g. a loading state in a button).

issue_title: Optional update migration: provide-initializer not working correctly
author: JoostK
comment_body:
The migrated code is doing exactly what the original was doing; the `deps` array is expected to be consumed as factory parameters otherwise they aren't used at all. Only depending for their request to have a side-effect is arguably a bad practice.

I don't think this warrants a change in the migration; note that migrations cannot in the general sense account for all possible coding patterns and I'd argue this is one such pattern.

issue_title: Optional update migration: provide-initializer not working correctly
author: alxhub
comment_body:
I'd agree - the passing of the `deps` to the `useFactory` function is not type-checked in the previous API, but that's what happens at runtime. The failure after the migration is surfacing an issue that's present in the original code but not caught by type-checking.

If we wanted to preserve this behavior, we could cast the factory function to `any`:

```ts
const initializerFn = ((() => () => {}) as any)(inject(Sentry.TraceService));
```

However, I think this would be to the detriment of other usages of `deps` which are truly parameters to the factory function. I don't think we should change the migration in that case.

issue_title: Mistake in the description of equality comparison for linked signal
author: bst-celum
comment_body:
The documentation still feels a bit misleading to me and might cause some confusion.

The original idea seems to be that the `email` signal should only update when the `id` of the `activeUser` changes. However, in the current example, the `email` signal produces an object with an `id` property, which feels out of place.

Here are the main issues I see:

- Type Mismatch: The `email` signal is producing an object `{ id: ... }` instead of a `string` (the actual email). This doesn't align with what you'd expect given the name and context.
- Confusion Around Equality Check: The equality function is comparing the `id` property of the result of the computation, but the description implies that it’s tied to changes in the `activeUser` signal (the source). This creates a disconnect between the intended and intuitive behavior - that might be expected from the description - and what’s actually happening in the code.

In my opinion, it would be better to link to the equality section of "plain" signals https://angular.dev/guide/signals#signal-equality-functions and only showcase here that the same can be done with a `linkedSignal` without an example around it.

I still think that the documentation is misleading, also including the last changes.

author: DigitalBrainJS
comment_body:
If the issue is with the xhr adapter, then the problem is not with Axios itself, but with the implementation of `XMLHttpRequest` on the target platform. The problem may occur if the request size is not calculated. You can try manually setting the `Content-Length` header if it's not set automatically. If this wouldn't fix the issue, there's probably nothing we can do about it in the context of the xhr adapter, as it's most likely an internal platform issue.

https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/11853

If you still have this issue after upgrading to node, you might want to make sure [keepAlive](https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/1846) is enabled. I had a similar issue where axios was raising ENOMEM errors even though the memory usage never exceeded 500mb (out of 4096mb).

The malicious content sent to the web browser often takes the form of a JavaScript segment, but can also include HTML, Flash or any other type of code that the browser executes. The variety of attacks based on XSS is almost limitless, but they commonly include transmitting private data such as cookies or other session information to the attacker, redirecting the victim to web content controlled by the attacker, or performing other malicious operations on the user's machine under the guise of the vulnerable site.
Cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities occur when:

1. Data enters a web application through an untrusted source. In the case of DOM-based XSS, data is read from a URL parameter or other value within the browser and written back into the page with client-side code. In the case of reflected XSS, the untrusted source is typically a web request, while in the case of persisted (also known as stored) XSS it is typically a database or other back-end data store.


2. The data is included in dynamic content that is sent to a web user without validation. In the case of DOM-based XSS, malicious content is executed as part of DOM (Document Object Model) creation, whenever the victim's browser parses the HTML page.

issue_title: Security vulnerability
author: wraithgar
comment_body:
There is no security vulnerability here.  The code is contained wholly in the `isURLSameOrigin` code.  That code simply compares two urls and returns a boolean if their origin is the same.  The url objects created therein that have their `href` attributes set are never returned, and thus couldn't possibly be serialized or displayed to the end user.

The PR addressing this is generally a good code cleanup, but it's just that.  No CVE should be made from this and folks who are following along should not concern themselves about a security issue here.

author: chinesedfan

@spawnrider Thanks for your detailed information and screenshots. Note that call stacks(hover your mouse on the initiator column of the browser's network panel) only show the situation when just sending the request, which doesn't mean "actions.js:180" will never be called. It's a kind of history, instead of future behaviors.

- When the first request is send, "actions.js:180" has not been called yet, or at least not in the upper call stack.
- When the second request is send, it is there, which means the second request is send by inner function code of "actions.js:180".

If added a breakpoint at "actions.js:180", you will see it stops twice. One is when the page is loading. And the other is after I submitted the admin name and password. If you add a log statement after "actions.js:180", I bet it will be printed twice. In summary, nothing is wrong.

issue_title: Axios send the same request twice and ignore the first response, only receives the second response.
author: VidurMalik
comment_body:
For everyone facing this problem and using Sagas / Actions, the problem might be in your sagas. Sagas might get yielded twice which will lead to the action being called once, but the web request executing twice. A potential solution is to use `takeLatest`/`takeLeading` rather than `takeEvery` in your sagas (https://redux-saga.js.org/docs/api/index.html#takeleadingpattern-saga-args)

If this doesn't work, maybe look at if your sagas are being mounted twice. @chinesedfan

issue_title: perf: Improved pointer events related performance when the sidebar is docked with a large library open
author: dwelle
comment_body:
Hey!

> However, this detour helped me identify the real bottleneck. I noticed that although pointer events no longer triggered React re-renders, there was still some unusual behavior. After some more investigation, I found that the App component frequently changes the --ui-pointerEvent CSS variable to block other elements' interactivity, and applying these changes was the root cause of the lags.
> 
> My proposed solution is to remove these changes while maintaining the same UX (i.e., no interaction with outside elements during canvas interaction). During a canvas pointer up event, we capture the pointer events to the canvas itself. This ensures that all other outside elements will be non-interactive until a pointer up event. I tested this solution and it provides the same UX as before, though there could be some edge cases I'm not aware of. Unfortunately, I have noticed the tests are failing because pepjs, the library that polyfills pointer events to jsdom does not properly support the capturing phase for pointer events. Still, I think this idea is worth considering at least.

Interesting find, and solution! I've mocked the API for tests since we weren't testing this part of the UI behavior anyway. We'll see if it bites us in the future.

I've also kept the old logic in case the `setPointerCapture` is not supported — while it has a good browser support, on mobile it's not quite universal, and a pointer handling shouldn't be something we'll completely break in those cases.

--

I'll need to go through the LibraryMenu changes tomorrow, but so far, looking good 👍.

issue_title: perf: Improved pointer events related performance when the sidebar is docked with a large library open
author: dwelle
comment_body:
Alright, so [first](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/pull/9086/commits/9d90808c87a82994c515a6341523afefbb2d3efe) I removed the `pendingElements` update optimizations you made because there were issues with updates (e.g. when you change color of current selection, it wouldn't catch the change), and also it seemed it wasn't worth the effort.

But then I realized that in multiplayer scenarios it will rerender the `LibraryMenuContent` on every remote change because `cursorButton` will be `up` most of the time, so I [reintroduced](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/pull/9086/commits/3e9707196311e87e733a674ef3d2818e53ab57bf) the memoization but made it a bit more robust — which also made it more complicated / slower. But it seems there's some non-trivial perf benefit.

That said, there are some non-intuitive things happening, such as that without the optim (technically _with_ the optim as well) there are more rerenders when the remote client is dragging an element you _don't_ have selected (which should bail) as opposed to editing your own selection. Unclear why, something that can be investigated later.

Thus, the quest for making Library sidebar more optimized continues, I would say — but I'm glad we've made a good step toward optimizing it :).

Thanks! ❤️

issue_title: feat(`FileStatusList`): Use `TreeView`
author: mstv
comment_body:
Thank you for the detailed feedback. I am aware of the TODOs.

`TreeView` has several limitations, particularly icons:
`StateImages` are limited to 14 (only a runtime error when trying to use a higher index). `StateImages` are scaled in a special way.
`Images` work better. But it looks ugly if some nodes have no icon.
With `OwnerDrawAll`, one needs to draw everything including tree lines, which feels like implementing the tree view control from scratch, what I do not want to do.

Tooltips are automatically provided - if `Text` matches the owner-drawn length. I saw the wrong selection highlight length, too. I am adapting this.

> Should changed submodules be in modified status group? Now they are separated.

"Sort by status" is a TODO yet and should yield the same ordering as before. New subgroups or changes in the ordering should be added in a follow-up.

> Separate the flat/tree setting?

I prefer a one-stop shop. A "tree / flat" toggle could be useful in addition.
Later, we should add a toolbar with sort options and filtering.
FormCommit and artificial commits could use a separate sorting setting.

author: gerhardol
comment_body:
I have no need to defend the change, but I guess I will explain why I prefer it this way.
Everything can be improved.
It is possible to change the behavior back to the 3.5 so when opening separate instances, they use the FileHistory.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6248932/148295394-6f9f59e6-2a1a-47d7-92fe-d47a01adc8fb.png)

I want to set FileHistory as deprecated, remove it at some point together with other forms like Compare.
This is quite some extra code to maintain.

Note that FileHistory (both before and in master) can be used to show history for several files or folders.

>     1. Before it was a clearly identifiable different view. Now it's difficult to distinguish to a normal instance

How to make this clearer? 
Suggestion in next question.

Personally, I hardly use the extra instance, just filters in current Browse (`F` in Diff/Tree) then clear the filter (`Shift-Ctrl-F` in grid).
 
>     2. There is a lot less space to see the diff and blame. And you always have to move the split separator. Sometimes a diff was difficult to read, so now that you can't see the whole file and have a blame view, it will be worst :(

Some shortcut to collapse the left panel as well as the FileStatusList?
(Could be default when open with file filter).

>     3. You loose the "View" tab (that I sometimes I preferred to use because I found the blame aggressive when you move your mouse and the grey selection change)

The "filtered file" is preselected in Diff/Tree.
You can view the file instead of blame in Tree tab with `B` (as well as Blame in Diff).

>     4. You no more are able to identify quickly which instance is file history (and when you want to switch quickly and often during an investigation or when you want to clean the instances opened, its a pain) lost in all similar windows
> I think we need to reproduce this behavior (ie. changing the title of the application) when the "Path filter" is enabled

The title is already adjusted when there is a file filter, FileHistory could be added too. Or just put the filtered path name first?

>     5. Maybe when we open a new instance to enable the "Path filter", the left panel should be hidden

See 2.

>     6. I don't know if it make sense also to filter the file list also

The file is preselected, also when you change commit (unless you select a file that is in the newly selected commit too), so I do not see a need here.
If something, add the file status list filter.
 
>     7. Perf: It takes more time to open the file history in another window. And because it's a full GitExtension instance, it also fetch in background if enable, do the `git status` that could take a lot of CPU on big repositories.

With the repo loading tweaks in master, I find opening Browse similar to FileHistory before.
(Also not using separate instances much.)

>     8. Q: Is there a possibility to open the old window? I though we would keep it...

See above, but I would like to prepare to remove.

>     9. I'm pretty sure the "Filtering" icon is not enough visible for legacy user that will have it enabled when doing "File History" as usual (and that we will have some issues opened). And a dropdown menu (like the stash button) to disable quickly the filters could be an improvement...

Dropdown for Advanced filter would be nice.
(I settled with implementing the shortcut eventually, there were too much going on.)

>     10. When blame is enabled, it's strange the way to come back to the "diff" view. You need to click again on the file.

My intention was that you only do the blame temporary that you go to FileTree for longer term blame.
I find this convenient.

>     11. When you use "Blame this revision" or "Blame previous revision", you come back to the diff view
>         ![blame](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/460196/148285926-6be2f99e-eff3-43be-9cae-dac37f054b56.gif)

That could be changed.

>     12. Q: Where are all these options:
>         ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/460196/148283985-bd1984d4-1715-44b8-9a17-03116141a7ab.png)

Should be added to Settings

>     13. When you are in blame but you change the commit selected, you switch to the diff (I think that's the problem) even if  the blame icon is still enabled.

Same as 11, all changes go back to diff.

issue_title: Invalid date for format "YYYYMMDDHHMMSS"
author: maggiepint
comment_body:
I think the format that you want is 'YYYYMMDDHHmmss'

Right now you're using the months token (MM) twice, and the second token is parsing and setting months a second time, as a number greater than 12, ergo your date is invalid. The proper token for minutes is 'mm'.
In addition SS is a token for fractional seconds, but I believe you have whole seconds which are represented by 'ss'.

The following works fine:

``` js
moment('20160307133625','YYYYMMDDHHmmss').format()
"2016-03-07T13:36:25-06:00"
```

author: ichernev
comment_body:
Well, setting the global locale only changes the locale for newly created moments. And because you have one test object, it creates.

Now the other thing is that when you clone a `moment` object by `moment(m)`, you preserve the locale of `m`, so even though the locale for new moments is `en` you keep the `de` locale that `m` has (`this.start` and `this.end` in your example).

@msevestre Yeah of course, although I think my solution may be out of date now, I made it work in my code and moved on, I think a later version of moment might have fixed it. Nevertheless, my fix is:

```js
import moment from 'moment'

This is what I'm doing, and it's working for me, but as I say it may no longer be necessary.

issue_title: moment cannot always parse moment default formatted negative years
author: icambron
comment_body: Yeah, there's probably a bug in the ISO parser there. Would be happy to take a fix.

issue_title: moment cannot always parse moment default formatted negative years
author: ichernev
comment_body:
That is a weird one. If you use `toISOString()`, then it correctly outputs `-000001`, which can then be correctly parsed.

`format()` uses a default format with `YYYY`, that would then output `-0001`, which can then not be strictly parsed into ISO, because ISO forbids 4 digits with a sign, and states you should use more (and in moment we stick with 6 digits in this case).

On the other hand there is the problem that `YYYY` does not parse any leading signs, so if you have year : `y < 0 || y > 9999` it won't be parsed correctly with `YYYY`, even though it was formatted with `YYYY`.

If we change the way `YYYY` parsing works, it will break for cases like `'20151209', 'YYYYMMDD'`, because `YYYY` can in theory consume more than 4 digits (if the input was bigger), and this case is far more likely than the case with an year bigger than `9999` or negative. Only supporting negative is going to fix the issue presented here, but won't fix years above `9999`, or below `-9999`.
- So if the concern is `format() produces something unparsable` we can fix format to use `YYYYYY` instead for weird years.
- If the issue is that format('YYYY') can not be parsed with 'YYYY', then we can only (maybe) fix that for `y in (-9999, -1)`, because the other option is impossible.
- If the issue is that `-0001-...` is not valid ISO ... not sure what to do here, as the docs don't really specify anything about years below 1583, except "the parties should reach an agreement". So if the agreement was to use ISO string (`toISOString` not `format`), this is a non-issue.

issue_title: moment cannot always parse moment default formatted negative years
author: marwahaha
comment_body: I think both 1 and 2 are important. I feel like being able to parse whatever the default to `format` is an important guideline. Plus, the symmetry is important (format->YYYY should parse with YYYY).

issue_title: Library uses code from stackoverflow.com
author: mattjohnsonpint
comment_body:
It will not affect your license.  We are licensing all code in this project under the MIT license.  All contributions to this project are released by their contributors under that license.  It does not matter where the technique was learned from.

With regard to actual code snippets, those are being used in accordance with the fair use doctrine.

Additionally, Creative Commons is a _content_ license.  It only applies to the _publication_ of the material, such as when viewing the source code. If you took large chunks of code from a CC licensed project and pasted them on your blog without any attribution, then you would be in violation.  But you can put that same source code into your project and ship your product under whatever license you wish without any attribution whatsoever.

At least that's my interpretation. I am not a lawyer.

There are plenty of discussions on this on StackOverflow's Meta site.

issue_title: Security issue with the usage of \\ inside replace method
author: gilmoreorless
comment_body:
I think you've misunderstood what the linked code does. The CodeQL link is warning about incomplete **escaping**, but the `unescapeFormat` function does the _opposite_ of escaping — it's stripping away certain escaping characters **then passing them to the `regexEscape` function** to do the proper escaping.

Additionally, `unescapeFormat` only runs on small tokens that have already been broken apart by the regex at https://github.com/moment/moment/blob/18aba135ab927ffe7f868ee09276979bed6993a6/src/lib/format/format.js#L4-L5

Static code analysers can only make inferences based on patterns, but won't always know the full context of the code. They're very helpful for catching potential bugs, but they do also have false positives. This is one of those times.
Blindly following the reports of a static analyser 100% can sometimes lead to problems, in the same way as completely ignoring them. Context always has to be taken into account.

issue_title: React-Native Release Builds, Deep Crash when changing locales
author: fbartho
comment_body:
The referenced lines are "automatically" trying to require modules at runtime, but the [loading locales docs](https://momentjs.com/docs/#/i18n/loading-into-browser/) indicate that if you're using a Package Manager like JSPM, you can load locales by `import "moment/locale/fr`. Since we need the react-native package manager to "know" that the file must be imported, we tried that style of import so that the Packager can "see" all files that have to be bundled in.

Ultimately, our import lines looked like this:

```typescript
import moment from "moment";
import "moment/min/locales"; // Import all moment-locales -- it's just 400kb
import "moment-timezone";
```

The exact implementation of `require()` is injected by the runtime you're working with, and that's definitely something that behaves significantly differently between Debug & Release builds.

In react-native, there are also several different flavors of Release-mode JavaScript Bundling, including all-in-one-file, all-in-separate-files, and RAM Bundles. Each of these also change how require works. Debug `require()` connects to the [Metro Bundler](https://facebook.github.io/metro/) running on a local http server. This is probably is very similar to the webpack/jspm/other debug servers, which is probably why aliasing require doesn't cause problems in that environment.

issue_title: React-Native Release Builds, Deep Crash when changing locales
author: fbartho
comment_body:
## My Fix Proposals:

A. Delete the `aliasedRequire` entirely if that's not how you're supposed to do things any more + tweak install instructions about it?
B. Detect react-native vs browser (`navigator` isn't available in react-native, but there are other techniques here), and behave differently depending on which situation we find ourselves in? eg. if react-native && DEV then print a console.error if the locale is theoretically supported, but hasn't been `required` yet (+ update docs).
C. Move the `aliasedRequire` from a local variable in that function to a "semi-global". `moment.aliasedRequire`, that way we could inject a no-op/do-nothing function so that `aliasedRequire` can't cause react-native to crash hard anymore.

author: joe06102
comment_body:
if anyone meets such errors as **"can not find module './locale/xxx' in react-native production build"**，

**try to import the locale files manually**.

eg: 
```javascript
import * as zh from 'moment/locale/zh-cn';
```

As far as I know, dynamic require is not supported in the **Metro** packager, which causes such errors.

I spent 2 days and got it working now, check this out:

https://github.com/puppeteer/puppeteer/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#running-puppeteer-on-google-cloud-run

You need to enable Google Cloud Run to always allocate dedicated CPU for you otherwise the process will exit as soon as a response is returned without waiting for the puppeteer event to come back.

A bit more troubleshooting since my initial post, this page is pulling data from a database and Puppeteer is losing focus on the field that doesn't get completed (if I add a chai expect in after each page.type, when it fails to fill out a field completely the screenshot it takes does not have focus on the input field).

I think what may be happening is puppeteer is just running too quickly and it begins filling in the fields, at some point during this the page finishes getting data from the server and refreshes the page (not a browser refresh.....I'm using React & Redux, so the state updates with the fetched data and refreshes the display).

This loss of focus is not ever seen by a user (because they won't select an input as quickly as puppeteer will) so it's only an issue with puppeteer itself, I can force it to work fine if I make puppeteer wait 500ms after landing on the page (which is enough time for DB calls to resolve locally but may not work in my remote environment).

I've also tried waiting for networkidle and what not, but I'm getting to this page with a click action not a network call so I don't think I can easily wait for networkidle.

Any suggestions on how best to work around this issue? I don't like waiting for a static time because it will just introduce test flakiness in different environments.

comment_body:
> Any suggestions on how best to work around this issue? I don't like waiting for a static time because it will just introduce test flakiness in different environments.

@Nagisan I'd try a few options here:
- if the page fetches something over network and you know the url it loads, you can subscribe to the [`requestfinished`](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/puppeteer/blob/master/docs/api.md#event-requestfinished) event and wait for the request to finish
- if you have access to the website codebase, you might issue a call to `console.timeStamp` with some label, e.g. `console.timeStamp('mynicelabel')`. In puppeteer, you'll get a related [`metrics`](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/puppeteer/blob/master/docs/api.md#event-metrics) event with a `'mynicelabel'` title

author: rienheuver
comment_body:
I was having trouble with the page not having fully loaded yet. The fix for me was to add this as second parameter to `page.goto`:
```
{waitUntil: 'networkidle2'}
```
This makes it wait until there have been no more network requests for the last 500ms. So the total `page.goto` looks like this:
```
await page.goto('https://example.com', {waitUntil: 'networkidle2'});
```
Hope this helps someone out :smile:

issue_title: [Bug]: Failed to launch the browser proccess using Same userDataDir & Different Profile Directory (concurrent)
author: OrKoN
comment_body:
```
& 'C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe' --user-data-dir='C:\{{path_to}}\chrome-data' --profile-directory=profile1

& 'C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe' --user-data-dir='C:\{{path_to}}\chrome-data' --profile-directory=profile2
```

this does not actually launch a second browser process. In the second command, you should see the output like `Opening in existing browser session.` indicating that it detected the previously launched process and handled the command there closing the second process. Puppeteer on the hand always launches a new process and the browser instance as alive as long as the process is alive and does not support switching between profiles. Each Chrome browser process wants a singleton lock of the user-data dir, that's why you see a failure. You can start the two profiles via the commands and connect the browser instance using https://pptr.dev/api/puppeteer.puppeteer.connect/  or you can create temporary profiles using https://pptr.dev/api/puppeteer.browser.createbrowsercontext/. For now, we do not have plans on changing this behavior.

issue_title: [Bug]: Failed to launch the browser proccess using Same userDataDir & Different Profile Directory (concurrent)

comment_body: Forgot to mention that you can achieve the behavior similar to the behavior via direct commands by supplying all args yourself and setting https://pptr.dev/api/puppeteer.launchoptions/#ignoredefaultargs on the launch process but the result will be the same, the commands will be handled by the first process and the second process will be closed.

author: haixiangyan
comment_body:
For me, I will recommend @jsnanigans solution, using

```js
  await page.focus(usernameInput)
  await page.keyboard.type(username)
```

Using @hzoo solution is OK for small script, but is not very maintainable for big project. The main problem of this solution is that you are actually injecting a JavaScript code in the website. That means it will not work for TypeScript, async/await, external variables. For example

```js
  const myVar = 'hello'
  await page.evaluate(() => {
    const a: string = 'hello' -> Syntax Error, not work for TypeScript.
    
    console.log(myVar) -> Variable myVar is not defined

    async a() {} -> Some browser hasn't support await/async syntax yet
  })
```

comment_body: @pragyandas You can't just append two binary blobs like this to concatenate pdfs. The resulting blob is not in the right format. Or use [a library](https://www.npmjs.com/package/pdf-merge) that does this for you if you don't mind writing to disk.

We encountered the same issue when we redeployed our service to Google Cloud App Engine after bumping the node version from 16 to 20. What solved it for us was adding the [--no-cache](https://cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/standard/php-gen2/specifying-dependencies) option when deploying.

> > 
> 
> Hey @AeShevch,
> 
> Instead of headless=true, use headless="new". headless=true is going away. Reference [here.](https://developer.chrome.com/articles/new-headless/#new-headless-in-puppeteer).
> 
> Also, can you please mention what was the key thing that led to fixing the issue? Was it setting PUPPETEER_SKIP_CHROMIUM_DOWNLOAD env variable to true or headless=true? Because I deployed my app on Vercel & got the same error. Vercel does not support Docker images on hobby plan. So do you have any workarounds for me?
> 
> Thank you 💓

`headless: true` is not going away. It is a way to opt in now, but in a future release specifying `headless: true` will simply use the new headless mode instead of the old one. https://github.com/puppeteer/puppeteer/blob/0d4aab828ac92f6269d6af1dad923fc9daa4158c/packages/puppeteer-core/src/node/LaunchOptions.ts#L26-L36

issue_title: page.evaluate() is leaking memory
author: jpgklassen
comment_body:
**Update:** After a ton of troubleshooting, I've determined that the memory leak is happening in `page.evaluate()`. When this function returns, every variable declared within the function remains in memory. The callback function that was passed to `page.evaluate()` is also stored in memory, in the form of a string! It makes no difference if I call `page.close()` and `browser.close()` after every single `page.evaluate()`... the variables still continue to accumulate in memory until the program runs out of memory and crashes. I've even tried manually running the garbage collector after every `page.evaluate()`, but it doesn't get rid of the variables.

**This is a big problem for those of us who are using puppeteer for web scraping!!**

issue_title: [DDP] Use NCCL allocated memory for gradient bucket
author: syed-ahmed
comment_body:
> Perhaps we can maintain a segment-address-to-bool dictionary to record the registration status of segments? (Edit: I see that registeredSegmentHandles_ already does so)

Yeah, may be we can make `registerSegment` a no-op when a segment is already registered. However, that function was originally implemented for the `TORCH_NCCL_USE_TENSOR_REGISTER_ALLOCATOR_HOOK` path: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/3f5ed0568886ca4c144213a27918019a2e3ebab0/torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/ProcessGroupNCCL.cpp#L311-L328. So not sure if it would break any internal workload.

issue_title: [DDP] Use NCCL allocated memory for gradient bucket
author: kwen2501
comment_body: Yeah, I am adding a flag `errorOnRereg` to `registerSegment` API with a default value of true. In `registerMemPool`, we can set the flag to false.

issue_title: [DDP] Use NCCL allocated memory for gradient bucket
author: syed-ahmed
comment_body: We should also add a `deregisterMemPool` in ProcessGroupNCCL::shutdown(), and I think that will make this diff complete :).

issue_title: [DDP] Use NCCL allocated memory for gradient bucket
author: kwen2501
comment_body:
I left `deregisterMemPool` out because I wasn't sure when it would be safe to call it --
- If we call it before `ncclCommFinalize`, at that point the collectives are still executing, would the dereg create any side effect? (not very likely but I cannot rule it out)
- If we call it after `ncclCommFinalize`, at that point could some resources of the communicator be freed already and cause the dereg call to fail? 

I'd need more confirmation before adding in that call.

issue_title: [DDP] Use NCCL allocated memory for gradient bucket
author: syed-ahmed
comment_body:
Looking at NCCL source, it looks like `ncclCommDeregister` is just cleaning up some cache. Also `ncclCommDestroy` calls the cleanup function as well. I think it's safe to put it after `ncclCommFinalize` as `ncclCommDestroy` happens after `ncclCommFinalize`.
```
ncclCommDeregister -> commDeregister -> regCleanup
ncclCommDestroy -> commReclaim -> commCleanup -> commFree -> ncclRegCleanup -> regCleanup

```

issue_title: [DDP] Use NCCL allocated memory for gradient bucket
author: kwen2501
comment_body: Cool, thanks much for checking! I added the dereg after finalize!

author: sterrettm2
comment_body:
> The perf numbers LGTM. Seems CI failures are related. Could you please fix them first?

I've spent a while looking at the test failure, and I think the test itself is wrong.

The input array has some duplicate elements.
The test is then comparing the indices from the argsort for exact equality, but isn't using stable=True.
So it then uses x86-simd-sort, which isn't stable and which orders identical elements in a different way compared to the current implementation.
This causes the test to fail, even though both argsorts seem to give valid results.
To test this, I tried reordering the input array using the indices from both the reference sort and x86-simd-sort, and the resulting arrays match exactly.

I assume it is okay for these indices to not match exactly, since stable is set to false in this test.
I modified the test to handle testing sort/argsort differently; I'm not super familiar with this testing code, so I'm not sure if this change is reasonable

author: sterrettm2
comment_body:
`equal_sort_checker` does not have special logic for checking the inputs. I assume you are referring to this code:
``` 
self.assertEqual(
    ref_inputs[0][actual.indices],
    ref_inputs[0][correct.indices],
    atol=atol,
    rtol=rtol,
    equal_nan=True,
    exact_dtype=exact_dtype,
) 
```
If that's the case, what this code is doing is checking that the actual and correct indices are 'argsort equivalent', in the sense that if we reorder the original inputs with the indices from the argsort, we get identical results. Currently the only thing checking the inputs is that shared check that the inputs have not been modified

So, it turns out the initial test failures were caused by reference_in_float being True, which meant that for fp16 one of the sorts upconverted to fp32, causing one sort to use the standard method and one to use XSS. 

Because of this, simply changing that parameter causes the CPU tests to pass, even without custom equality checking. I've made a version of the patch without the custom equality checking, to see if it passes the full test suite.

This is much simpler, so if it passes all the tests would you prefer it as the solution? Technically it still leaves the potential for another sorting related patch to have this problem, but I think that currently isn't an issue. This essentially just enforces that eager and inductor behave exactly the same.

```
Section "Device"
  Identifier "Configured Video Device"
  Driver "dummy"
  VideoRam 16384
EndSection

Section "Monitor"
  Identifier "Configured Monitor"
  HorizSync 5.0 - 1000.0
  VertRefresh 5.0 - 1000.0
  ModeLine "1920x1080" 23.53 1920 1952 2040 2072 1080 1106 1108 1135
EndSection

Section "Screen"
  Identifier "Default Screen"
  Monitor "Configured Monitor"
  Device "Configured Video Device"
  DefaultDepth 24
  SubSection "Display"
    Depth 24
    Modes "1920x1080"
  EndSubSection
EndSection
```

For further details regarding Xorg configuration please see: https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/xorg

> Are we expecting user to only do in certain directories? 

Yes. When we talk about "running inside a project" we mean exactly this.

> What I would expect is that the function that invokes scrapy should work wherever I invoke it.

It works as documented, by finding the current project. If there is no current project it obviously can't find it.

> There should be a way for me to pass scrapy.cfg file path if the underlying code can't find its location properly.

"can't find its location properly" (together with some of the earlier comments and proposed "solution") sounds like you expect Scrapy to find some random scrapy.cfg in some unrelated directory. I don't think that's possible to implement.

All of this is very old HTTP/1.0 code, which is not used by default for quite some years (you need to change the `DOWNLOAD_HANDLERS` setting for "http" from `scrapy.core.downloader.handlers.http.HTTPDownloadHandler` to `scrapy.core.downloader.handlers.http.HTTP10DownloadHandler` to use it, losing HTTP/1.1 support). I don't think it's possible to actually port it, so we can either merge the non-overridden parts of `twisted.web.http.HTTPClient` into `scrapy.core.downloader.webclient.ScrapyHTTPPageGetter` like we did with `twisted.web.client.HTTPClientFactory` in #4165, or deprecate and drop the code.

If we want to drop the code, we could extract it into a separate project but that one won't be maintained. Or we could simply drop it and maybe suggest something to use instead (a custom download handler based on... something? or, more likely, just an older Scrapy version).

issue_title: ValueError: Cannot use xpath on a Selector of type 'json'
author: Gallaecio
comment_body:
I find it interesting that you were able to use XPath to parse HTML within a JSON structure before.

If you are looking for a workaround, downgrade parsel to <1.8.

As for a long-term solution, I am inclined to say that this is how things should work.

If you have `{"html": "<html><title>foo</title></html>"}`, you do not use `response.xpath("//title")`, you use `response.selector.jmespath("html").xpath("//tittle")` (or, starting with the upcoming Scrapy 2.9, `response.jmespath("html").xpath("//tittle")`).

author: GeorgeA92
comment_body:
> I find it interesting that you were able to use XPath to parse HTML within a JSON structure before. On parsel 1.6.0 and older - application add extra `>

` tags that "make" it.. possible to use css xpath selectors (attempt to "get" valid html as browser does) ```python from parsel import Selector selector_json = Selector(text='{"a":"1"}') print(selector_json.getall()) # parsel 1.6: ['

{"a":"1"}

'] # parsel 1.8: [{'a': '1'}] # <-converted to dict, we see ' instead of original ", most likely expected to receive str here" #print(selector_json.css('*::text').getall()) print(selector_json.css('p::text').getall()) # parsel 1.6: ['{"a":"1"}'] # parsel 1.8: ''' print(selector_json.css('p::text').getall()) File "\parsel\parsel\selector.py", line 680, in css raise ValueError( ValueError: Cannot use css on a Selector of type 'json' Process finished with exit code 1 ''' ``` > If you have {"html": "foo"}, you do not use response.xpath("//title"), you use response.selector.jmespath("html").xpath("//tittle") (or, starting with the upcoming Scrapy 2.9, response.jmespath("html").xpath("//tittle")). In case if server return json response with.. html inside it's variables - Selector will be was able to parse it's html content by xpath/css selectors without any additional data transformations: ```python text2 = '''{ "prod_1": "
1$
", "prod_2": "
2$
", "prod_3": "
3$
"} ''' selector_html = Selector(text=text2) print(selector_html.css('div.price::text').getall()) # parsel 1.6: ['1$', '2$', '3$'] # parsel 1.8: ''' print(selector_html.css('div.price::text').getall()) File "\parsel\parsel\selector.py", line 680, in css raise ValueError( ValueError: Cannot use css on a Selector of type 'json' ''' ```
